message.content: Add "upload an image from my computer" to the Nxeon webmail SIGNATURE editor in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15, Prisma). Today the signature rich editor's image button only accepts a URL (via a browser prompt) — because the sanitizer strips inline `data:` images (and email clients block them anyway). Add a real file-upload path: the user picks an image from their PC, we host it, and insert an ABSOLUTE https URL into the signature so it renders both in the composer and in recipients' inboxes. ## Study & reuse first (do NOT run git or `npm run build`) - `app/api/chat/upload/route.ts` + `lib/chat-attachment.ts` (`validateImageBytes`, `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`) — the existing image-upload pattern: multipart formData, validate bytes by signature (rejects SVG/non-images), store bytes in Postgres, rate-limit. REUSE `validateImageBytes` + `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`. - `app/api/chat/attachment/route.ts` — how stored image bytes are served back (content-type, response). - `components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx` — the `contentEditable` signature editor + its toolbar. Find the current "Insert image by URL" button and the selection save/restore helper it uses (`execCommand('insertHTML', …)` / range restore). The image insert must go at the saved cursor range. - `lib/mail/render.ts` `safeHtml` — confirms https `` is allowed (the absolute upload URL will be https and must survive sanitization; `data:` is stripped — that's why we host). - How the app builds absolute URLs (APP_URL / `process.env.APP_URL` / `renderAppUrl` in `lib/email-render.ts`) — the returned image URL MUST be absolute (e.g. `https://nxeon.cloud/api/mail/signature-image/`) so it loads in external email clients. ## YOU OWN prisma/schema.prisma this wave Add a model to store uploaded signature images (mirror `ChatAttachment`): e.g. `SignatureImage { id String @id @default(cuid()); userId String; mime String; sizeBytes Int; data Bytes; createdAt DateTime @default(now()); @@index([userId]) }`. After editing, run `npx prisma generate` (LOCAL only — do NOT run `prisma db push`; the parent applies it). ## Implement 1. **Upload route** `app/api/mail/signature-image/route.ts` (POST, `runtime="nodejs"`): `requireUser()` (owner must be signed in), rate-limited (reuse `checkRateLimit`), multipart `file`; cheap size guard then `validateImageBytes` (reject SVG/non-images, cap `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`); store bytes in `SignatureImage` for the user; return `{ url: "/api/mail/signature-image/" }`. Cap images per user (e.g. delete the user's oldest when over ~20) so it doesn't grow unbounded. 2. **Serve route** `app/api/mail/signature-image/[id]/route.ts` (GET, public — email recipients have no session, so NO auth here; the id is an unguessable cuid): return the bytes with the correct `Content-Type`, a long `Cache-Control` (e.g. `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`), and `Content-Length`. 404 if missing. 3. **Editor UI** (`MailSettings.tsx`): change the image toolbar button to open a hidden ``. On pick: show a brief "Uploading…" state (disable the button), POST to the upload route, then insert `` at the SAVED selection range (reuse the existing range-restore so focus loss from the file dialog doesn't drop the insert point). Surface size/type errors inline. KEEP a secondary "paste URL instead" affordance (small link/menu) so the old URL path still exists, but make **upload from computer the primary action**. Everything themed to the dark Nxeon UI. 4. The inserted `` must pass `safeHtml` on save/preview/send (it will — https src). Don't change the signature save/send flow otherwise. ## Constraints - No new npm deps. Additive schema only; `npx prisma generate` but NOT `db push`. Do NOT touch billing/resize/terminal/cpanel/migration/backup files. Do NOT run git or `npm run build`. - Validate images by bytes (never trust the client MIME); reject SVG (XSS vector) — `validateImageBytes` already does this, reuse it. The serve route is public by design but returns only stored image bytes with an image content-type. - Write/Edit may time out on a hook — fall back to Bash heredocs and verify. - Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx prisma generate >/dev/null 2>&1; npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files). Report: the schema model, the upload + serve routes (and how the URL is made absolute + why the serve route is public), the editor UX change, the per-user cap, and confirm the inserted image survives `safeHtml` and renders in outgoing mail.

content.text: Clean — prisma generate succeeded and tsc reports no errors (the filter left no output, meaning zero errors anywhere). ## Summary Added an "upload an image from your computer" path to the Nxeon webmail signature editor. It hosts the picked image and inserts an absolute https URL so it renders in the composer and in recipients' external inboxes. ### Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`) New `SignatureImage` model mirroring `ChatAttachment`: `id (cuid) / userId / mime / sizeBytes / data (Bytes) / createdAt`, `@@index([userId])`. Bytes live in Postgres. Ran `npx prisma generate` locally (no `db push`). ### Upload route — `app/api/mail/signature-image/route.ts` (POST, `runtime="nodejs"`) - `requireUser()` (401 if not signed in) — only the owner uploads. - Rate-limited via `checkRateLimit` keyed on `sig-image::` (15/min). - Multipart `file`; cheap `file.size > MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` guard, then `validateImageBytes` (byte-signature sniff — rejects SVG/non-images, caps 5 MB, stores the sniffed MIME, never the client-declared one). - Stores bytes in `SignatureImage`, then returns `{ url: "/api/mail/signature-image/" }`. - **Absolute URL**: built from `appUrl()` in `lib/email-render.ts` (`process.env.APP_URL ?? "https://nxeon.cloud"`), so it loads in recipients' mail clients that have no notion of our origin. - **Per-user cap**: `MAX_IMAGES_PER_USER = 20` — after each insert, `findMany` ordered newest-first with `skip: 20` and `deleteMany` on the overflow (best-effort, never fails the upload). ### Serve route — `app/api/mail/signature-image/[id]/route.ts` (GET, public) Returns the stored bytes with the allow-listed `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, plus `nosniff` + `default-src 'none'; sandbox` CSP hardening. 404 if missing. **Public by design**: the URL is embedded as `` in outgoing mail and fetched by recipients/Gmail's image proxy who have no session; safe because `id` is an unguessable cuid (no path traversal) and the response only ever emits image bytes with an image content-type, never executable HTML/JS. ### Editor UX (`components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx`) - The toolbar image button is now the **primary "upload from your computer"** action: it saves the caret (`saveSel()`) then opens a hidden ``. During upload the button is disabled and shows a spinner ("Uploading…"). - On pick: POSTs to the upload route, then inserts `` at the **saved selection range** via the existing `insertHtml`/`restoreSel` helper, so the file dialog's focus loss doesn't drop the insert point. - Kept a secondary **"URL"** affordance (small link beside the image button) that still prompts for an https image URL — now also inserts with `max-width:100%`. - Size/type errors surface inline in a themed red strip above the editor; both insert paths escape the URL into the attribute (`escAttr`). All styling matches the dark Nxeon UI. ### safeHtml / outgoing mail The inserted `` uses an absolute **https** src, which passes `safeHtml` (only `javascript:/vbscript:/data:/blob:/file:` schemes are neutralized; `style` is preserved), so it survives save, preview, and send unchanged. Hosting (vs. inline `data:`) is exactly why it renders in recipients' inboxes. The signature save/send flow was not otherwise touched, and no billing/terminal/cpanel/migration/backup files were modified.
